body.p: In the article by Jain et al., “Patient-Reported Outcome Measures and Health-Related Quality-of-Life Scores of Patients Undergoing Anatomic Total Shoulder Arthroplasty,” which appeared in the September 2019 issue of the journal (J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2019 Sep 4;101[17]:1593-600; doi: 10.2106/JBJS.19.00017), the authors discovered an error in the algorithm that they had used to derive the Short Form-6 Dimensions (SF-6D) scores from the Short Form-36 (SF-36) scores. They subsequently recalculated the SF-6D scores and repeated the statistical analysis. This repeat analysis demonstrated that there was essentially no change in the preoperative SF-6D values but that there was a significant change (improvement) in the 1-year postoperative SF-6D scores. This change resulted in a difference in the authors’ findings relative to the responsiveness of the SF-6D with regard to the effect size and the standardized mean response to a change in the outcomes after anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty. Specifically, the responsiveness of the SF-6D was large rather than moderate and therefore was comparable to that of the EQ-5D. As a result, several changes were needed throughout the article.

In addition, during the process of correcting the original article, it was noted that 2 subjects were inadvertently included when they should have been excluded: 1 with 1-year follow-up and 1 without 1-year follow-up. Lastly, an error was noted in Table III: there were 3 “yes” responses at the initial preoperative evaluation.

For these reasons, the Editor decided that retracting the original article was appropriate. JBJS has requested that the authors resubmit a corrected version of this manuscript, which will undergo the copyediting process and will be posted as soon as it is ready.
